Riding the tower, you are at a disadvantage because this weapon does not have a large amount of range an you cannot be as mobile around the tower as a sploosh-o-matic or a tentatek. Instead, clear out enemies on and around the tower from below; and support those riding the tower by zoning them and distracting them.

Well, the game actively does actually make it harder for you to rank up to S. Penalties for losing are harsher, and basically the game is asking for you to carry your team by yourself. And that's necessary to get into S rank - you need to be that much better than the A and A+ ranks.

I remember the first time I got into S, I had the same difficulties as you, where I'd get up to A+ 98, 99, etc and then lose one game (and subsequently 15 points) because I ended up with a shit team. The truth is that every time I got up there, I'd pressure myself too much to get kills and win 1v1s over pushing the objective. So personally I looked good, but I wasn't playing smart.

I recently took an alt account to S after I got my main to S+, and after a couple months of playing in S and S+ lobbies, the ride back to S, even with weapons I didn't normally use, was much easier, as a result of the combination of my increased ability to aim and my mindset in-game to play smart over get kills. 

As for how to play smart over getting kills, I'd say it's very situational and a bit difficult to explain in all instances. In simplest terms, the objective is your baby and eliminate anyone who threatens it. But if it is not threatened (aka some enemy is just chilling in your spawn trying to catch a straggler, but your team has beakons set up), don't go back to take that guy out.

Something I learned when climbing from S to S+ and C- to S again is that you WILL win games when you feel you are the best player in the match and apply that mindset to the way you are playing.
